page.layout: One page of running text, one column. Page number at the top right. Running head centred at the top, in Hebrew. No marginal notes. Nothing printed below the last line except the scan's digitiser credit, which is left out.

main_text.p: Magnum opera pretium effet, hanc expositionem posse ex Rabbinorum libris firmari. R.Bechai in principio Genesis fol.5.col.2.scribit; Nomen quadraginta duarum literarum defumi ex primo & secundo versu principii Genesis, a littera ב vocis בראשית usque ad ב vocis ובהו, quae sunt 42 literae, ex quarum varia & multiplici combinatione, Cabalistis nota, fit nomen expositum per 42. literas. Nomen autem duodecim literarum, fit ex triplicata combinatione Nominis יהוה. Videamus etiam varia Talmudistarum & Rabbinorum testimonia.

In Codice Talmudico Kiddufchin, cap.4. fol.71. legitur: Nomen quatuor literarum sapientes tradiderunt discipulis suis semel in septimana: alii dixerunt, bis. Rabh Nachman filius Jitzchak assensit illis, qui dixerunt Semel, juxta illud: Hoc est nomen meum לעלם in seculum, Exod.3.15. scriptum est לעלם absque Vau in medio, quasi לעלם Ad abscondendum, quod abscondi manere debuerit. Rabba existimans publicis concionibus nomen tetragrammaton explicandum esse; illi senex quidam regesit, scriptum esse לעלם Abscondi debere. Rabbi Abhina objecit: Scriptum est, Hoc est nomen meum; Item, Et hoc est memoriale meum, Exod.3.13: Ergo duo fuerunt nomina? Respondit Deus: Non sicut scribor, ita pronuncior: Scribitur per Joth He Vau He, nempe יהוה, sed pronuncior per Aleph Daleth, id est, אדני. Amplius docuerunt Rabbini: Nomen duodecim literarum principio tradiderunt cuilibet homini: cum autem multiplicarentur homines perfrictae frontis & impudentes, tradebant illud tantum verecundioribus & modestioribus ex genere sacerdotali: (nempe, ut eo benedicerent populo post sacrificium matutinum, addit Scholiastes).

page.notes: The Hebrew forms לעלם (with the Vau absent or present) and the Hebrew at the top are hard to read on the scan; they are copied as they appear, with [?] on the uncertain running head. The Tetragrammaton forms are copied as printed. The last line ends in a small stray mark after "Scholiastes)", which is not clear. Long s is rendered as s throughout, and the printed "fcribor" and "assensit" are normalised to "scribor" and "assensit". The Greek/Hebrew words in the first paragraph are as printed.
